svg.aria-label: A path MTU black hole: a narrow link in the middle, big packets dropped, and the ICMP message that would explain it dropped too

g.text: small packets: the request, ACKs, small.txt (6 bytes)
The server resends in 1,400-byte packets, and everything works.
The server never hears why. It resends the same big packet, again and again: 0 bytes arrive.

ol.li: Small packets cross the narrow link without trouble. The connection opens, the request goes out, and a tiny file comes back.

A big packet with Don’t Fragment set (TCP always sets it) doesn’t fit. The router drops it, and sends back an ICMP “fragmentation needed” message, with the size that would fit. The sender shrinks its packets: that’s path MTU discovery.

But if a firewall on the way throws away ICMP (“it’s just ping, isn’t it?”), the sender never finds out. It waits, resends the same packet, and waits again. Small things work; big things hang for ever. That’s a black hole.

figure.figcaption: The path MTU black hole, as breakit.sh blackhole builds it.
